findings.F1: Step 5's main measure is on the side the idea predicts, with a next-day unusual move in the short direction of +0.79 % per case (t 3.26, 538 cases on 355 days), but the supporting check fails: the larger-|forecast| half is 0.18 % worse than the smaller half; in folds B and C the 126 cases (96 days) average +1.31 % (t 1.77).
findings.F2: The day's width against the 30-day swing carries the effect: among the cases, the widest third gives +3.38 % (t 2.17, 33 cases, 27 days), while the middle and narrowest thirds give -0.20 % (t -0.17) and +0.68 % (t 0.62).
findings.F3: Closeness to the high grades the wrong way, and it dilutes the forecast:
findings.F4: The effect holds across years in folds B and C (2019 +1.95 %, 2020 +1.99 %, 2021 +0.64 %, 2018 +0.05 % on 9 cases), and on the main coins it is positive on BTC (+3.35 %), ETH (+2.01 %) and ZEC (+1.73 %) and near zero on LTC, XMR and XRP. It is uneven by coin, not tied to one period.
findings.F5: The mirror side shows the same reversal. In the profile, closes in the bottom quarter of the range are followed by rises: in the short direction, -2.14 % (t -1.82, 40 cases) for closes 75–90 % down the range and -1.03 % (t -1.55, 34 cases) for the bottom tenth. A near-high close on a day whose return was in the lowest third falls the most (+3.04 %, t 2.06).
findings.F6: Size against cost: the total move of +0.67 % per case is 3.0 times the 0.22 % cost of a trade. The book still lost to holding (Sharpe 0.52, 0.03 below holding's) because it was in a position on only 3 % of coin-days.

ideas.idea: In a choppy, agitated market, a day closing near its high falls over the next day, and the fall is larger the wider the day's range against the coin's 30-day swing of daily returns.
ideas.consequence: A trader in a choppy, agitated coin would sell a day that closes near its high for one day, sized by how wide the day was against its usual swing rather than by how close the close sits to the high.
ideas.name: choppy agitated wide high-close fall
